text:
alex: hey everyone  I'm Alex, starting today. quick startup questions: where do I post badge/hardware pickup vs request infra access? also which bots should i subscribe to as a new hire?

sam: hey Alex, welcome! :wave: Badge/hardware -> #people-ops. Infra/access (Okta/AWS/VPN) -> #help (create a short ticket). Join #new-hires and #devex. Mute noisy bots unless you need them.

tara: welcome! For laptop image or replacement, open a ticket in #help and tag "hardware". For repo/AWS role access, request in #eng-infra or DM @infra-lead. To opt into the onboarding checklist, DM onboarding-bot and run `/onboard subscribe`.

onboarding-bot: Tip: run `onboard checklist` to get VPN, Okta, repo links, and your buddy info. Use `onboard links` to pin quick links. :robot_face:

devin: etiquette note: use threads for follow-ups so channels stay readable. Never paste credentials in Slack. Use the ticketing flow for anything sensitive. Use :thumbsup: reactions for quick acks.

jess: slack prefs tip: star channels you use, mute the deploy and monitoring bots until you need them, and pin onboarding docs to the channel for quick access. DM me if you want help cleaning your channel list.

alex: thanks! one more: where do I request dev API keys for the hosted API? want to avoid leaking anything in slack.

sam: never post secrets in Slack. Request dev keys via dev-portal (link in the onboarding checklist) or open a request in #security using the template. If urgent, DM @security and include the ticket link.

mike: deploy-bot -> subscribe only if you're on call or deploying. Otherwise mute it per-channel. Monitoring alerts go to #eng-sre only for on-call folks.

tara: small workflow tip: if your question touches multiple teams, start in the most relevant channel and @mention the team (e.g., @eng-infra). For quick personal help, use threads or DMs. Your buddy should be your first contact for day-to-day questions.

alex: super helpful, thanks all :thumbsup:
